title: Disrupting or restoring cell communication should trigger or suppress cancer

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Disrupting or restoring cell communication should trigger or suppress cancer

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The shrinking-Self view of cancer predicts that interfering with physiological communication among cells should be able to trigger cancer and restoring it should suppress cancer, and that the relevant parameter (communication) is spread over considerable distance rather than confined to single cells as genomic damage is.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This view predicts that interference with (or restoration of) physiological communication among cells should be able to trigger (or suppress) cancer and that the relevant parameter (communication) is spread out over considerable distance and not confined to single cells (e.g., genomic damage).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self”. Scope: Metazoan tissues; tested so far in amphibian models

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.63

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Communication and tumour phenotypes can be measured, and public cancer datasets permit association and some perturbation analyses. The causal trigger-and-suppression prediction requires interventions and spatial physiology that current public datasets cover incompletely.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across perturbations of gap junctions, membrane voltage, and long-range physiological coupling, estimate effects on transformation and tumour burden, and compare rescue by restored coupling against genomic-damage and cell-autonomous models.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Human observational data confound communication loss with tumour progression.

Amphibian intervention data may not be deposited or broadly generalizable.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.48
data existence: 0.65
analysis feasibility: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The prediction names a manipulation, a readout, and a spatial signature, so it is testable. The manipulations that exist are published tadpole experiments, scattered in papers and indexed by Xenbase, not a multi-species perturbation matrix. Those papers can speak to the amphibian scope and do not cover metazoan tissues at large. Distance and genomic confounds remain inside the published designs, which makes the available test partial.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Interrupt physiological coupling and score tumor-like incidence; restore coupling and score suppression; vary the distance between the perturbation and the affected cells. Triggering at a distance and suppression on restoration would support the prediction; purely cell-autonomous genomic effects with no distance dependence would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Voltage changes alter transcription, which confounds a pure coupling mechanism.

Open cancer genomics resources lack a communication-block perturbation.

Published tests are amphibian and largely from one research program.
